summary:
I audited the Hevy side of Training (HevyTab and its sub-tabs, LogHevyWorkoutModal, RoutineModals/routineForm, HevyPRList, the Body tab, Exercises/GIF picker, TrainingCalendar, NextSessionBanner, the sync button and hooks, Strava, hevyApi/trainingApi/stravaApi) plus the hevy-api edge function's payload contract. Everything here was read and cross-checked end to end; nothing was run against live data. `tsc --noEmit` is clean. The findings below are behavioural bugs, not type errors.

The four most serious:
1. **Strava connect is broken.** The OAuth redirect goes to `#/training`, but the only code that exchanges `?code=` (StravaWidget) is mounted only on Developer → Connections, so the code is never exchanged.
2. **Log workout sends keys Hevy rejects.** The modal's payload includes exercise-level `index`/`title`/`supersets_id` and set-level `index`. CLAUDE.md documents that the same keys return a 400 on routines, so this almost certainly fails the same way (not checked against a live Hevy call). The modal also ignores exercise type (duration/distance) and saves `end_time = start_time`.
3. **Personal records are computed from at most 1,000 arbitrary sets.** `fetchHevyPRs` has no pagination and no order. It also treats assisted-exercise assistance weight as a PR.
4. **Workouts are ordered by the wrong timestamp.** `fetchHevyWorkouts` orders by `hevy_created_at` (when the record was created in Hevy) instead of `start_time`. Several screens take `[0]` as "latest workout" or take a fixed 200-row slice. Home already re-sorts locally to hide this.

Other groups:
- **Wrong dates:** the calendar, Progress history and the PT coach cut the date from the UTC timestamp (`slice(0, 10)`), while the Workouts tab and Daily use the local day. Workouts starting between 00:00 and 02:00 Oslo land on different days on different screens.
- **Misleading calendar:** past plans (including every projected recurring slot) always show red "missed", even on days a workout was logged. The calendar also only loads the latest 200 workouts, so older months look empty.
- **Same concept, different code paths:**
  - "Next session" is computed two ways, and the Training banner ignores recurring templates.
  - Bodyweight is read from four different sources on four screens.
  - There are three set renderers; the workout detail can't show duration/distance sets.
  - There are two est1RM formulas that disagree above 12 reps.
  - Log workout re-implements the routine editor's exercise search, set rows and payload builder without its type awareness or strict payload.
- **Silent no-ops and data risks:**
  - Routine "Delete" is local-only, and the next Sync restores the routine.
  - A saved current program whose routines no longer exist gives an empty Progress view with no prompt.
  - The Body modal carries prefilled values to a newly picked date and can't clear a field.
  - The edge function ignores a failed read of the existing row, which re-opens the documented body-measurement data-loss path.
  - Fixing a broken GIF doesn't show until the card remounts.
  - "Close out" hard-deletes a task with no confirmation.
- **Fragile reads and cleanup:**
  - `hevy_sets` is paginated without `.order()`.
  - Several full-table reads have no pagination.
  - Two hevyApi functions and one hook are dead code.
  - Sync hooks live in the wrong files.
  - One table is cached under five different limits.

Files: /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/api/hevyApi.ts, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/components/LogHevyWorkoutModal.tsx, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/api/stravaApi.ts, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/components/StravaWidget.tsx, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/components/TrainingCalendar.tsx, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/components/NextSessionBanner.tsx, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/components/BodyMeasurementModal.tsx, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/components/BodyMeasurementsTab.tsx, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/components/HevyWorkoutCard.tsx, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/components/HevyWorkoutDetail.tsx, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/components/HevyPRList.tsx, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/components/RoutinesTab.tsx, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/exerciseMedia.tsx, /home/user/Project_Daily/src/features/training/hooks/useProgressData.ts, /home/user/Project_Daily/supabase/functions/hevy-api/index.ts.

findings.title: Strava OAuth redirect lands on /#/training, but the only ?code= handler is mounted on Developer → Connections, so connect never completes
findings.evidence: stravaApi.ts:5 `const REDIRECT_URI = `${window.location.origin}${window.location.pathname}#/training``. The exchange lives only in StravaWidget's effect (`const code = params.get('code') … connectWithCode(code)`), and StravaWidget is rendered only in ConnectionsTab.tsx:148 (grep finds no other mount). TrainingPage/StravaTab never render it. After consent Strava sends the user to `#/training?state=&code=…&scope=…`, nothing reads the code, it expires, and the Connections card still reads 'Connect Strava'.
findings.fix: Point REDIRECT_URI at the page that owns connections: `#/developer?tab=connections` (the widget's parser already splits the hash on '?'; make it tolerate the extra `tab=` param). Alternatively move the code exchange into useAppBootstrap() so it runs on any shell route. Either way the handler and the redirect target must live in the same place. Add a one-line comment tying the two together.

findings.title: Log workout payload contains keys Hevy's schema rejects (exercise index/title/supersets_id, set index), ignores exercise type, and re-implements the routine editor
findings.evidence: handleSave builds `exercises: …map((e, ei) => ({ index: ei, title: e.template!.title, notes: null, exercise_template_id, supersets_id: null, sets: e.sets.map((s, si) => ({ index: si, type, weight_kg, reps, … })) }))`. hevy-api forwards it verbatim: `hevyRequest('POST', '/v1/workouts', …, { workout: payload })`. CLAUDE.md's Hevy payload traps say exercise = `exercise_template_id, superset_id, rest_seconds, notes, sets (NO index/title)` and sets have `NO rpe/index`, each 'a real 400'. routineForm.ts:119-122 records the same rule ('any extra key triggers a "… is not allowed" 400 … no exercise index/title, no set index … superset_id is singular'). This modal sends `index`, `title` and the misspelled `supersets_id`. It also renders only Weight/Reps for every exercise (grid `Type | Weight (kg) | Reps`), so a plank, run or carry can't be logged. The routine editor already has `setFieldsForType`, `SetRow`, `ExerciseSearch` and a strict `formToPayload`; this file carries its own combobox, set grid and module-level `_setId/_exId` counters.
findings.fix: Build the workout payload with a strict builder beside `formToPayload` (e.g. `workoutFormToPayload` in routineForm.ts). Emit exactly `{title, description, start_time, end_time, is_private?, exercises:[{exercise_template_id, superset_id, notes, sets:[{type, weight_kg, reps, distance_meters, duration_seconds, custom_metric, rpe}]}]}`. Reuse `ExerciseSearch` and `SetRow` with `setFieldsForType(template.type)` so duration/distance exercises get the right inputs. Mirror `stripNullRepRange`-style key sanitising server-side in handleCreateWorkout as a belt-and-braces guard. Verify against one live POST before shipping (the repo's no-speculative-schema rule).

findings.title: fetchHevyPRs reads hevy_sets with no pagination or order, so all-time PRs come from an arbitrary first 1,000 sets
findings.evidence: `const { data: sets } = await supabase.from('hevy_sets').select('exercise_template_id, weight_kg, reps, hevy_exercise_id').eq('type', 'normal').not('weight_kg', 'is', null)`: no `.range()` loop and no `.order()`. supabase/config.toml sets no max_rows override, so PostgREST's default 1,000-row cap applies. The same file already paginates hevy_sets for exactly this reason (fetchMuscleVolume:153-169, fetchTrainingHistory:238-267: 'never silently truncated at the 1000-row PostgREST cap'). At about 18 working sets × 3 sessions a week, 1,000 rows is only about 4-5 months. After that, 'All-time heaviest lift' and 'Top 5 lifts' silently ignore whichever sets fall outside the arbitrary first 1,000.
findings.fix: Paginate with `.order('id').range(offset, offset+999)` until a short page, like fetchMuscleVolume. Better: move the aggregation server-side with a SQL view/RPC (`SELECT DISTINCT ON (exercise_template_id) … ORDER BY exercise_template_id, weight_kg DESC, reps DESC`) that also returns `count(DISTINCT hevy_workout_id)` for times_performed. That also removes the large `.in('id', exerciseIds)` URL.

findings.title: fetchHevyWorkouts orders (and filters) by hevy_created_at, not start_time; several screens take [0] as 'latest workout' or a fixed 200-row window
findings.evidence: `.order('hevy_created_at', { ascending: false })` and `if (from) query = query.gte('hevy_created_at', from)`. hevy-api stores `hevy_created_at: workout.created_at` (the time the Hevy record was created). That differs from `start_time` for back-dated or imported workouts, including anything logged through LogHevyWorkoutModal with a past date. Consumers: WorkedMuscles `useHevyWorkouts({ limit: 1 })` → 'last trained'; the PT coach `recent[0]` → 'SON ANTRENMAN'; the Workouts list page order; the calendar's 200-row window. Home already works around it (`[...workouts].sort((a, b) => workoutDate(b).localeCompare(workoutDate(a)))`), which shows the source order is known to be wrong. hevyApi.ts:411 even claims fetchHevyWorkouts 'already prefers start_time', which it does not.
findings.fix: Order by `start_time` descending with `{ nullsFirst: false }` plus `hevy_created_at` as a secondary key (index `hevy_workouts_user_id_start_time_idx` exists). Make from/to filter the effective date with the same `or(start_time range, and(start_time.is.null, hevy_created_at range))` used elsewhere. Then delete Home's local re-sort and fix the misleading comment.

findings.title: Workout/activity day is cut from the UTC timestamp in the calendar, Progress history and PT coach, but uses the local day in the Workouts tab and Daily
findings.evidence: TrainingCalendar `workoutDay = toDateStr(w.start_time ?? w.hevy_created_at)` where `toDateStr = iso.slice(0, 10)`, and the same for Strava `toDateStr(a.start_date)` (strava-activities stores Strava's UTC `a.start_date`). fetchTrainingHistory `dateByWorkout.set(w.id, (w.start_time ?? w.hevy_created_at).slice(0, 10))`, with a comment saying it deliberately matches the calendar. PostgREST returns timestamptz as `…+00:00`. Meanwhile HevyTab.tsx:142/179 and daily TrainingCard use `formatLocalDate(new Date(w.start_time))`, and the calendar compares against local `ymd(date)`. A session starting between 00:00 and 01:59 Oslo shows on day D in Workouts/Daily but on D-1 in the calendar, Progress sessions/weeks (a Monday 00:30 workout counts in the previous week) and the PT coach's 'last 7 days'.
findings.fix: Add one helper, e.g. `workoutLocalDay(iso)` → `formatLocalDate(new Date(iso))`, next to dateFormat.ts. Use it in TrainingCalendar (workouts and Strava), fetchTrainingHistory, ptCoachApi and useProgressData's `toStr`. Update the comment in hevyApi.ts:216-218.

findings.title: Calendar paints every past plan red 'Plan missed', even on days a workout was logged; recurring templates are projected onto every past matching weekday
findings.evidence: `function planTone(dateStr, todayStr) { if (dateStr === todayStr) return 'warn'; return dateStr > todayStr ? 'info' : 'danger' }`. The tone never looks at whether that day has a workout or Strava activity. plansByDate projects recurring training templates over the whole visible range (`while (cursor <= end) … projectRecurringBlocksForDay(...)`), so a Mon/Wed/Fri template makes every past Mon/Wed/Fri in the month show a red 'Plan missed' dot next to a green workout dot. Freeform workouts don't auto-close their task (server matches on routine_id only), so their one-off block also stays red.
findings.fix: Compute the plan tone per day as `past && (workouts.length || activities.length) ? 'success' (or neutral 'fulfilled') : past ? 'danger' : …`, passing `day.workouts`/`day.activities` into the tone function. For recurring projections on past days, show them only when unfulfilled (or in neutral), and update the legend ('Plan done' vs 'Plan missed').

findings.title: Calendar loads only the latest 200 workouts/activities regardless of the visible month, while plans are fetched by range, so older months look empty or all 'missed'
findings.evidence: `const { data: workouts = [] } = useHevyWorkouts({ limit: 200 })` and `useStravaActivities({ limit: 200 })` ignore `rangeFrom/rangeTo`, while `useTrainingBlocks(rangeFrom, rangeTo)` is range-scoped. Combined with TRN-H04 (ordered by hevy_created_at), paging back past the 200th workout shows months with plans but no workouts. `today` is also memoised once (`useMemo(() => …, [])` at :535), so a PWA left open overnight keeps yesterday as 'today'.
findings.fix: Fetch workouts by the visible range: `useHevyWorkouts({ from: rangeFrom, to: rangeTo, limit: 500 })` after TRN-H04 makes from/to filter start_time. Do the same for Strava (`fetchStravaActivities({from,to})`). Refresh `today` on focus/visibility, e.g. reuse the useAnchorDate pattern.

findings.title: 'Next session' is computed two ways: the Training banner ignores recurring training templates; Home and the calendar include them
findings.evidence: NextSessionBanner uses only `useTrainingBlocks(today, to)` (one-off time_blocks), and its docstring says 'the soonest future time_blocks row'. useTodayOverview.nextTraining adds `templates.filter(t => t.category === 'training')` projected day by day, and TrainingCalendar also projects recurring templates. For a user whose plan is a recurring Mon/Wed/Fri template, Home says 'Next training: Push · Mon 16:30' while the Training page banner shows nothing, or a one-off session weeks later.
findings.fix: Extract `useNextTrainingSession()` (the candidates logic now inline in useTodayOverview) into features/training/hooks. Use it in both NextSessionBanner and useTodayOverview. For a recurring hit, the banner opens `kind: 'schedule-block'` instead of `time-block`.

findings.title: Routine 'Delete' removes only the local row and the next Sync restores it; the confirm says it 'cannot be undone'
findings.evidence: The confirm copy is `'This removes it from your local data and cannot be undone.'`, followed by `deleteHevyRoutineLocal(id)` → `supabase.from('hevy_routines').delete().eq('id', id)`. Every Sync runs refreshRoutines, which re-fetches all routines from Hevy and upserts them (it deletes only ids Hevy no longer returns). The routine still exists in Hevy, so it comes back on the next Sync. It also leaves a dangling row in current_program_routines (no FK), which feeds TRN-M06.
findings.fix: Either remove the button and say 'Delete routines in the Hevy app; they disappear here on the next Sync', or keep a local 'hidden' flag instead of deleting. At minimum fix the copy ('Will come back on next Sync unless deleted in Hevy'), and also delete the routine's current_program_routines row in the same mutation.

findings.title: A saved current program whose routines no longer exist gives an empty Progress view with no prompt
findings.evidence: The gate is `if (currentProgramIds.size === 0) { … needsCurrentProgram: true }`, followed by `const activeRoutines = routines.filter(r => currentProgramIds.has(r.id))`. When every saved routine_id is gone (deleted in Hevy and reconciled by sync, or deleted via TRN-M05), size > 0 but activeRoutines = [], so currentExerciseIds is empty, templateIds = [] and there are zero decisions. needsCurrentProgram stays false, so ProgressOverview never shows the 'Select your current program' card; the table is just empty.
findings.fix: Gate on `validIds = [...currentProgramIds].filter(id => routines.some(r => r.id === id))`. If it's empty, return `needsCurrentProgram: true` plus a flag like `staleProgram` so the picker says 'Your saved program's routines no longer exist in Hevy — pick again'. Optionally add a real FK (`current_program_routines.routine_id → hevy_routines(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`; both are text).

findings.title: Body measurement modal: switching date copies the previous date's prefilled values, a cleared field can't be removed, and Edit + date change creates a second row
findings.evidence: (a) The prefill fills blanks only: `if (values[fd.key] === '' && row[fd.key] != null) values[fd.key] = String(row[fd.key])`. Values prefilled for today stay in the fields when the user switches to yesterday, so Save writes today's numbers onto yesterday. (b) handleSave skips empty fields (`if (raw === '' || raw === '.') continue`) and the server merge keeps stored values for omitted keys (`merged[key] = hasProvided ? Number(provided) : existing?.[key] ?? null`). Clearing a wrong value and saving silently keeps it, with no way to delete a value. (c) The Edit modal keeps an editable DateInput; changing the date upserts a new day and never removes the original row.
findings.fix: Track which fields came from prefill (e.g. `prefilledFrom: date` per field) and replace them when the date changes, instead of only filling blanks. Send explicit `null` for fields the user cleared and have hevy-api treat an explicit null as 'clear' (omit it from the Hevy body, write NULL locally). In edit mode make the date read-only, or implement move = upsert new date + clear old.

findings.title: hevy-api's body-measurement merge ignores a failed read of the existing row, re-opening the documented data-loss path
findings.evidence: `const { data: existing } = await supabase.from('hevy_body_measurements').select('*').eq('user_id', userId).eq('date', date).maybeSingle()`: the error is discarded. On a transient read failure `existing` is null, `merged` holds only the provided fields, and `hevyRequest('PUT', `/v1/body_measurements/${date}`, …, hevyBody)` replaces the whole day in Hevy. The local upsert then writes NULL for every other column. That is exactly the data-loss incident the MERGE comment above it describes.
findings.fix: `const { data: existing, error: readErr } = …; if (readErr) throw readErr` before building `merged`, so the call fails with a 500 and a toast instead of wiping the day.

findings.title: Workout cards never show exercise count or muscle chips: the list query never joins exercises/templates
findings.evidence: The card reads `workout.exercises?.length ?? null` and `ex.template?.primary_muscle_group`. fetchHevyWorkouts selects `'*'` from hevy_workouts only, and no code ever populates `HevyWorkoutExercise.template` (grep finds none). So `exerciseCount` is always null and `getMuscleGroups` always returns [], and both chips are dead UI on every card.
findings.fix: Either select `hevy_workout_exercises(exercise_template_id)` in the list query and join templates client-side (the templates query is already cached) to get the count and top 3 primary muscles, or remove the dead branches. Pick one; don't leave UI that can never render.

findings.title: Three separate set renderers; the workout detail shows duration/distance sets as '— × —'
findings.evidence: HevyWorkoutDetail's table has only 'Weight × reps' and RPE columns: `{set.weight_kg !== null ? `${set.weight_kg} kg` : '—'}{' × '}{set.reps !== null ? set.reps : '—'}`. Planks, cardio, carries and farmer walks (duration_seconds/distance_meters) render '— × —'. RoutinesTab.setLabel does handle duration/distance (`${s.duration_seconds}s`, `${s.distance_meters}m`), and LogHevyWorkoutModal edits only weight/reps. The same user concept, 'a set', is displayed three different ways.
findings.fix: Add one `formatSet(set, exerciseType?)` (in setTypeMeta.ts or a new setFormat.ts) that uses `setFieldsForType` to choose kg/reps/sec/m, and use it in HevyWorkoutDetail, RoutinesTab chips and anywhere else a set is shown. Replace the table's fixed 'Weight × reps' header with 'Set'.

findings.title: PR semantics disagree with the progress engine: assisted exercises rank by most assistance, failure sets are excluded, ties are arbitrary, and est1RM has no 12-rep cap despite claiming an exact match
findings.evidence: fetchHevyPRs keeps the max `weight_kg` per template regardless of template type (the template select is only `id, title, primary_muscle_group`). For `bodyweight_assisted`, weight_kg is the assistance, which the app's own progress model inverts (CLAUDE.md: 'less assistance over time = the improvement'). So the PR for Assisted Pull-up is your weakest session, and it enters 'Top 5 lifts by weight'. `.eq('type', 'normal')` drops 'failure' sets, which the engine counts as legitimate top sets. `if (!current || s.weight_kg > current.weight_kg)` keeps whichever equal-weight set arrived first (e.g. 100×5 instead of 100×8, with that older date). HevyPRList.est1RM has no rep cap, while progressAggregate.est1RM returns null above 12 and its comment says 'Matches the existing Personal Records feature's formula EXACTLY'.
findings.fix: Select `type` on templates and exclude `bodyweight_assisted` (or rank it by minimum assistance). Include 'failure' sets. Break ties by reps desc, then date desc. Delete HevyPRList's local est1RM and import `est1RM` from progressAggregate so one formula (with the 12-rep cap) is used everywhere.

findings.title: Bodyweight comes from four different sources on four screens
findings.evidence: The Hevy Body tab 'Latest' card and weight chart use `hevy_body_measurements` only (`useHevyBodyMeasurements(100)`). The Health Body section and HealthStatsPanel use `health_metrics.weight_body_mass` only. Progress/Relative Strength uses the union from fetchBodyweightHistory (manual wins). The PT coach and coach chat context use health_metrics only. A user who weighs on a scale synced to Apple Health and occasionally logs in Hevy sees a different 'current weight' on each screen, and the coach reasons on a number the Body tab doesn't show.
findings.fix: Create a `useBodyweightSeries(from, to)` hook built on fetchBodyweightHistory (the union rule already exists) and make the Body tab chart and Latest card, the Health Body section, HealthStatsPanel, ptCoachApi and coachContext all read it. Label the source per point (manual vs scale) instead of silently picking a table per screen.

findings.title: Body weight chart places fat % by index on the weight chart's x positions, and both series ignore real date gaps
findings.evidence: Weight x is `toX(xFrac(i, chartData.length))`, so the axis is evenly spaced by index and a 3-week gap looks like one day. Fat is `// Map fat data to same x positions as weight data (approx by index)`, i.e. `toX(xFrac(i, fatData.length))`. If fat was logged on 5 of 20 weight days, those 5 points are stretched across the whole width and line up with the wrong weight dates. The y labels show padded bounds (`paddedMax.toFixed(1)`), not real values.
findings.fix: Map x from dates (`(t - t0) / (tN - t0)`) for both series, or rebuild the chart on recharts with a shared time axis via useChartColors, matching the rest of Training. Label the real min/max. Better still, retire it in favour of the unified bodyweight series from TRN-M12.

findings.title: Log workout: end_time = start_time, a cleared date throws with no toast, the picked routine is never linked, and unpicked exercises are silently dropped
findings.evidence: `const start = new Date(dateTime).toISOString()` runs outside the try. Clearing the datetime-local field makes toISOString throw `RangeError: Invalid time value`: an unhandled rejection with no toast, and the button looks dead. `end_time: start` saves 0-minute workouts, which pollutes duration displays and Home's weekly minutes. TrainingCalendar's DayDetailPanel then renders a stray '0' via `{dur && …{dur} min}`. `routineId` is state only and never goes into the payload, so 'Start from routine' doesn't link the workout and the server's closeMatchingTrainingTask never runs. `.filter(e => e.template != null)` silently drops exercise rows where the user typed but never picked a match, sets included.
findings.fix: Validate the date (disable Log when invalid) and put the Date conversion inside the try. Add a Duration (min) field defaulting to 60 and set end_time = start + duration. Send routine_id if Hevy's POST schema accepts it (verify live); otherwise relabel the control 'Prefill from routine'. Block Save, or warn, when a row has sets but no exercise. Use `dur != null && dur > 0 &&` in TrainingCalendar.

findings.title: ExerciseThumb's failed flag never resets, so a fixed GIF doesn't appear until remount; manual overrides also depend on the 1,323-entry manifest loading
findings.evidence: `const [failed, setFailed] = useState(false)`; `if (!match || failed) return null`; `onError={() => setFailed(true)}`. Once a GIF 404s the card hides it, and saving a new override in ExerciseGifPicker (same TemplateCard) changes `match.gifUrl` but `failed` stays true, so nothing shows until the tab remounts. `match = db ? resolveExerciseGif(...) : null`: if the jsDelivr manifest fetch fails, even manually pasted GIF URLs vanish.
findings.fix: Store `failedUrl` and hide only when `failedUrl === match.gifUrl`. Resolve an override first without needing `db` (`overridesByTemplateId.get(templateId) ?? (db ? fuzzy : null)`).

findings.title: 'Close out' on a workout card hard-deletes the matched planned task and its block, with no confirmation, success toast or undo
findings.evidence: `<Button … onClick={() => deleteTask.mutate(matchedTask)}>Close out</Button>` → useDeleteTask → `deleteTask(id)` (hard delete; the linked time_block goes via ON DELETE CASCADE), with no successMessage. 'Close out' reads as 'mark done', but the plan disappears from the calendar, so it can never show 'planned and done'. The match is by `due_date`, which since migration 077 is independent of the block's date, so moved sessions don't match.
findings.fix: Mark the task done (useToggleTask/useUpdateTask with status 'done'), keeping history consistent with the Cancel-keeps-a-record convention, and make the calendar treat a done task's block as fulfilled (TRN-M02). If delete is kept, confirm and toast. Match on the linked block's date (useLinkedTimeBlock) rather than due_date.

findings.title: Fragile reads: hevy_sets paginated without .order(); templates/template muscles/routine sets unpaginated; very large .in() URL lists
findings.evidence: `.from('hevy_sets').select(…).in('hevy_exercise_id', exIds).range(offset, offset + PAGE - 1)` with no `.order()`. Postgres doesn't guarantee a stable order across LIMIT/OFFSET pages, so sets can be duplicated or skipped between pages. fetchHevyExerciseTemplates `select('*').order('title')` and its `hevy_exercise_template_muscles` join have no range, even though hevy-initial-sync imports Hevy's whole library (`/v1/exercise_templates?page=…&pageSize=100`). Past 1,000 rows, templates (or their secondary muscles) near the end of the alphabet silently disappear from Exercises, Log workout and routine search. `.in('hevy_exercise_id', exIds)` over about 500-700 uuid ids puts roughly 20-27 KB in a GET query string.
findings.fix: Add `.order('id')` to every paginated range loop. Paginate the template and template-muscle reads with a shared `fetchAllPaged(query)` helper. For the 182-day history, filter sets by a server-side join (`hevy_sets?select=…,hevy_workout_exercises!inner(hevy_workout_id)`) or an RPC keyed on the date window instead of shipping id lists in the URL.

findings.title: Writes don't refresh dependent views: body measurement save leaves Relative Strength/bodyweight stale; sync doesn't refresh the current program
findings.evidence: useUpsertBodyMeasurement uses `invalidates: [qk.hevy.measurementsAll]`, i.e. ['hevy','measurements']. fetchBodyweightHistory reads hevy_body_measurements under ['hevy','bodyweight-history',…] with STALE.long, so a new weight doesn't reach Relative Strength or the Progress bodyweight card until it goes stale. useIncrementalHevySync invalidates `[qk.hevy.all, 'taskGraph']`, but the sync can delete routines that qk.training.currentProgram still references (TRN-M06).
findings.fix: Invalidate `qk.hevy.all` (or add `['hevy','bodyweight-history']`) on a measurement save. Add `qk.training.currentProgram` to both sync mutations' invalidates (or fold it into the 'training' group they use).

findings.title: Dead API functions, window filter pasted 4×, sync hooks in the wrong files, the same table cached under 5 limits, 'this week' counted in 3 places
findings.evidence: fetchWorkoutExerciseTemplateIds has 0 callers and fetchWorkoutsWithTemplateIds is referenced only in a comment. useHealthMetrics has 0 callers. The `inRange`/`nullFallback` start_time-or-created_at filter is copy-pasted in four functions. useInitialHevySync lives in useHevyPRs.ts and useIncrementalHevySync in useHevyWorkouts.ts, while useHevySync.ts holds only useHevySyncState. useHevyWorkouts is called with limit 1, 20, 30, 50 and 200 (five cached copies of one table). 'Workouts this week' is computed separately in HevyTab WorkoutsSubTab, useWeekTrainingStats and daily TrainingCard.
findings.fix: Delete the dead functions. Add `workoutWindowFilter(fromISO, toISO)` and use it in fetchMuscleVolume/fetchTrainingHistory. Move both sync mutations and the sync-state query into useHevySync.ts. Add one `useRecentWorkouts()` (start_time-ordered, one limit) and a pure `countWorkoutsSince(workouts, weekStart)` shared by Training, Home and Daily.

findings.title: Set weight inputs use type=number, which on iOS with a comma decimal can drop '62,5'; the Body modal already solved this
findings.evidence: LogHevyWorkoutModal uses `<input type="number" step="0.5" …>` and SetRow uses `type="number" inputMode="decimal"`. With a Norwegian keypad the decimal key is ',' and a number input's value sanitisation turns '62,5' into '' (confirm on a device), so weight is saved as null with no warning. BodyMeasurementModal deliberately uses `type="text" inputMode="decimal"` plus `sanitizeDecimal` (comma → dot), and Food has a shared `DecimalInput`. That is three weight-entry behaviours in one feature.
findings.fix: Reuse the shared DecimalInput (or move sanitizeDecimal to shared/utils) for kg, rest and distance inputs in both the workout and routine editors.

findings.title: Calendar week cells are role=button divs containing nested buttons; the inner plan/workout buttons are about 18px tall
findings.evidence: `<div role="button" tabIndex={0} aria-pressed={isSelected} …>` wraps `<button … className="… px-1.5 py-0.5 text-micro …">` for each plan and workout. Nesting interactive controls inside a role=button is invalid ARIA (screen readers announce one control and swallow the rest), and the inner targets break the mandatory `min-h-[44px]` rule on the primary phone device.
findings.fix: Make the day header a real `<button>` (select day) and render plans/workouts as sibling buttons, not descendants. On phones keep the chips as non-interactive labels and put the tappable 44px rows in DayDetailPanel, which already lists them.
